what_happened: On a clear highway with no close lead vehicle (gap over 43 m), the policy braked hard for no visible reason, from 23.7 to 6.9 m/s, and fell about 9 m behind the recorded position. It also drifted about 1 m left of the recorded path, so actor 1, a replayed car passing in the left lane, drew level and the ego's front-left corner clipped it. Traffic behind also reached the ego, which counts as the recorded rear contact.

On an open highway with the nearest lead vehicle 40+ m ahead, the ego braked hard for no clear reason (23.7 to 6.8 m/s) while angling left out of its lane, against a RIGHT command at the end. Follower actor 1 closed in and swerved left to get around it, and the ego's front-left corner hit actor 1 as it came alongside.

On a clear multi-lane highway with no lead vehicle closer than about 44 m, the ego braked hard for no visible reason, slowing from 23.7 to 7.1 m/s, while its planned path drifted left. Its front-left corner swung into the left lane and hit actor 1, which was coming up alongside from behind at normal speed.

On a straight multi-lane highway, the ego was following a slower lead car (actor 48) in its lane and closing on it, with the gap falling from 18.6 m to 4.8 m by handoff at 4.7 s. Over the last 0.5 s the policy slowed only from 7.7 to 6.7 m/s and planned a swerve left instead of braking hard, so it hit 48 with its front at 5.2 s; the rear contact came after.

The ego was in a straight highway lane, accelerating toward a slower white utility truck (actor 2) ahead. When the policy took over at 4.7s the ego was doing 7.9 m/s with only a 7.2 m gap and closing at about 5 m/s. The policy braked hard, down to 3.8 m/s by 5.7s, but still hit the truck's rear with its front at a 4.6 m gap.

The policy took over at 4.7 s already 6.3 m behind a much slower pickup (actor 5) in its lane while closing at about 6 m/s. It braked right away (9.3 to 7.6 m/s in 0.5 s) but still hit the pickup's rear at 5.2 s. The ego was only 0.1 m from the recorded human path, so the lead in the simulation was slower or closer than in the real drive and the crash was set up before the policy took over; the ego was also rear-ended.

The policy took over at 4.7 s going 7.9 m/s with only about 7 m to a slower white box truck (actor 2) in the same lane. It braked (7.9 to 6.7 to 3.9 m/s) but too late and too softly, and hit the truck's rear at 5.7 s. The rear contact on the ego came after this front collision.

The ego went straight on a multi-lane highway and closed fast on the slower white utility truck ahead (actor 2) in its lane. The gap shrank from 12 m to 7 m while speed rose to 7.9 m/s before handoff. After the policy took over at 4.7 s it braked (7.9 to 3.9 m/s), but not enough, and its front hit the truck at 5.7 s. Actor 41 also struck the ego from behind.

The ego ran into the back of the slowing blue pickup (actor 5) directly ahead in its lane on a congested multi-lane road. The policy took over at 4.7 s with only a 6.3 m gap that was closing at about 6 m/s, and it was still going 9.3 m/s. It braked to 7.6 m/s, but too late, and hit the pickup at 5.2 s.

The ego was going straight in a busy multi-lane highway lane and closing on the blue pickup ahead (actor 5) at about 6 m/s. The policy took over at 4.7 s with only 6.3 m of gap, braked from 9.3 to 7.6 m/s, and still hit the pickup's rear 0.5 s later at 5.2 s (front collision; the ego was also rear-ended at some point).

In heavy, straight highway traffic, the ego closed on the slower white sedan ahead in its lane (actor 48), going from 18.6 m to 4.8 m while still on the logged trajectory. The policy only took over at 4.7 s with about 1 s to impact. Its plan swerved left and it barely slowed (7.7→6.7 m/s), so it hit the sedan's rear at 5.2 s.

The ego was following a slower white sedan (actor 48) in its lane, and the gap kept shrinking (18.6 m down to 4.8 m) while the recorded log was still driving. The policy took over at 4.7 s with about 1 s to impact and slowed only from 7.7 to 6.7 m/s, so the ego's front hit actor 48's rear at 5.2 s; the ego was rear-ended afterward.

The ego was already closing on slower lead car 12 in its lane before the policy took over at 4.7s, with the gap at 5.5 m and closing at about 3.5 m/s. Over the next 0.5s the policy planned a left lane change toward car 15 but braked only lightly (6.0 to 5.4 m/s), stayed on the recorded path (0.1 m off) and hit car 12's rear at 5.2s; the ego was rear-ended later.

The ego was going straight on a multi-lane arterial and closing on slower lead car 12 in its own lane. The gap shrank from 14 m to 6.8 m before the 4.7 s handoff. After taking over, the policy braked only gently (6.0 to 4.4 m/s in 1 s) and planned a leftward swerve instead of stopping, then hit car 12 with its front at 5.7 s, about 0.2 m from the recorded human path.

The ego was going straight in a highway lane, closing on slower lead vehicle 12 (gap 14.6→5.5 m while the ego went 7.1→6.0 m/s), when the policy took over at 4.7 s. The policy braked only mildly (to 5.4 m/s) and its plan drifted left without leaving the lane, and the ego's front hit car 12 at 5.2 s. The ego was still on the recorded human path (0.0 m off), so the setup it inherited may not have been avoidable: the lead car probably moved differently from the recording, and the ego was also rear-ended.

In slow freeway traffic, the ego closed in on lead car 12 in its lane: the gap shrank from 14.6 m to 5.5 m before the policy took over at 4.7 s. In the 0.5 s after that, the policy only eased off from 6.0 to 5.4 m/s, started planning a swerve to the left, and its front hit car 12 at 5.2 s. The ego was still on the recorded human path (0.05 m off), so the crash probably came mostly from car 12's simulated position or the setup at handoff, not from anything the policy chose.

The ego was following a slower car (actor 12) in its lane in heavy highway traffic. It took over at 4.7 s with only 6.8 m to the lead, slowed only from 6.0 to 4.4 m/s while its planned path began swerving left, and its front hit the lead car at 5.7 s. The rear contact came after this front impact.

The ego drove straight down the highway lane at about 11 m/s and closed on slower lead vehicle 1 at roughly 7.5 m/s; the gap shrank from 24 m to 5.3 m. The policy only took over at 4.6 s, when the gap was 5.3 m, and slowed only to 9.6 m/s, so it rear-ended vehicle 1 at 5.1 s. Separately, a vehicle also hit the ego's rear.

On a multi-lane highway, the ego was closing on a much slower lead vehicle (actor 1) in its own lane. The gap fell from 18 m to 7 m while the ego held about 11 m/s, and that was before the policy took over at 4.6 s. After handoff, the policy braked only lightly (11.1 to 9.7 m/s) and drew a late left swerve toward actor 36's lane, so its front hit actor 1 at 5.1 s. A rear contact on the ego came after that.

The ego went straight on a busy multi-lane road toward a slower lead car (actor 12) in its lane, with the gap closing at about 3.5 m/s. After handoff at 4.7 s (gap 6.8 m, about 2 s to contact) the policy braked only gently (6.0 → 4.4 m/s) and started planning a late swerve to the left, and it hit actor 12 head-on at 5.7 s. A rear contact on the ego came after that front collision.
